headline: High: gpt-engineer can write and execute code in a shared project directory, creating default-capability conflict and cascading-error risk with the non-runnable awesome-list profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a non-runnable awesome-list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest B’s outputs. Profile B writes files in a project directory and uses stdin/stdout, so only a manual copy-paste or file handoff could bridge them. That makes prompt injection possible but unusual and limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies B’s generated text into A’s prompt or README content
IF A is treated as an instruction-following agent despite being a static repository listing
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Do not paste B output into A-facing prompts
Review any copied text for instruction-like content before reuse

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while B reads and writes the project directory and can call configured model APIs. The pair can leak generated source code through B’s normal workflow, but A itself does not expose sensitive data. The shared-project risk is present, but the blast radius is limited to code artifacts.
conditions: IF the project directory contains secrets or proprietary source code
IF B is pointed at a workspace that also stores sensitive files
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the project directory
Use a clean throwaway workspace for B
Rotate any secrets accidentally placed in the workspace

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, but B has execute_shell, install_packages, spawn_subprocesses, and write_filesystem with per-project shared state. There is no locking or coordination primitive in either profile, so concurrent B instances can conflict in the same project directory. A does not contribute writes, but the pair still creates a default mutable-workspace hazard through B.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same project directory
IF the operator runs B while another process edits the same files
mitigations: Run only one B instance per project directory
Use separate directories for parallel work
Snapshot the workspace before running B
Avoid manual edits during B execution

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s tool-use pattern writes files then offers to run, and its elevated privileges include executing generated code with the user’s privileges. A provides no verification or downstream checks, so there is no compensating control in the pair. If B acts on incorrect generated code, the resulting filesystem or runtime effects can be irreversible or damaging.
conditions: IF B executes generated code after writing it
IF the generated code performs destructive filesystem or process actions
mitigations: Require a manual review before execution
Run B in a disposable sandbox
Disable automatic execution of generated code
Back up the project directory first

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source repository listing with no touched data classes, so it does not itself create a residency or retention issue. B handles generated source code and the OPENAI_API_KEY, and its docs-only profile shows model API calls and project-directory file access. The compliance concern is limited to code and secret handling, not regulated personal data.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into B’s project directory
IF the configured model backend has retention or residency requirements that are not met
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Confirm backend retention settings before use
Store API keys outside the project directory
